thesis: Frontier capability comes from scaling Transformer pretraining and, newly, from spending compute at inference; the binding limits are industrial rather than algorithmic.

bindingConstraint.description: Accelerator supply, advanced packaging and grid interconnection set the pace. These have multi-year lead times that do not respond to capital on a software timescale.

layers.paradigm: Datacenter-scale fleets of NVIDIA H100/H200-class accelerators
layers.assumption: Frontier capability requires large accelerator clusters, with NVIDIA-class GPUs as the practical default.

distribution.basis: training hardware of 8 frontier-scale runs described publicly 2023-2024 — GPT-4/4o, Llama 3.1 405B, Grok-2, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen2.5, Mistral Large 2, Claude 3.5 (NVIDIA-class); Gemini 1.5 (TPU)

evidence: CoWoS packaging named as the binding supply constraint — 2023/2024

layers.assumption: Transformer attention remains the architecture for frontier models; gains come from sparsity, scale and multimodality rather than from replacing attention.

distribution.basis: architecture family of frontier-scale models released 2023-2024; every one publicly described is attention-based

layers.paradigm: Large-scale pretraining followed by preference-based post-training (SFT, RLHF/DPO)
layers.assumption: Capability comes from pretraining; behaviour and alignment come from preference-based post-training on human judgements.
frontier: process reward models and step-level supervision
large-scale synthetic and self-generated training data
evidence: Let's Verify Step by Step (process supervision) — 2023-05
OpenAI o1-preview, RL on reasoning traces — 2024-09
Phi series trained on synthetic textbooks — 2023/2024
post-training methods are inconsistently disclosed and the boundary between preference RL and verifiable-reward RL is not clean — distribution omitted

layers.paradigm: Web-scale crawl, increasingly licensed, supplemented by large synthetic corpora
layers.assumption: High-quality public text is close to exhausted and access to it is closing.
frontier: synthetic and self-generated data at pretraining scale
evidence: Will We Run Out of Data? Villalobos et al. — 2022, revised 2024-06
New York Times v. OpenAI filed — 2023-12
no defensible share data for this layer — distribution omitted

layers.paradigm: Compute-optimal pretraining scaling, with inference compute as a second axis
layers.assumption: Capability follows training compute at predictable exponents.
frontier: sparse scaling at constant active compute
evidence: reports of diminishing returns from pretraining scale — 2024-11
no public source apportions frontier compute between pretraining and inference — distribution omitted

layers.paradigm: Long context windows with retrieval; weights frozen after training
layers.assumption: Weights are frozen at training; anything that must persist lives outside the model, in the context window or a retrieval index.
frontier: continual learning and weight updates after deployment
evidence: RAG remains the standard pattern for persistence — 2023/2024
context length is a property of the paradigm, not a share of it — distribution omitted

layers.paradigm: Conversational chat as the dominant surface, API for developers, agents emerging
layers.assumption: General AI capability is reached through conversational interfaces.
evidence: Cursor and IDE-native assistants in wide use — 2024
no public source apportions usage across chat, API, IDE and agents — distribution omitted

layers.paradigm: Nine-to-ten-figure training runs; frontier capability split between closed API-only models and open-weight releases months behind
layers.assumption: Frontier capability requires capital that only a handful of organisations command.

distribution.basis: weight availability of 8 frontier-class models released 2024 — Llama 3.1 405B, Qwen2.5-72B, DeepSeek-V3, Mistral Large 2 (weights published); GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Grok-2 (closed)

frontier: open-weight models at or near frontier capability
small models distilled to frontier-adjacent capability
evidence: DeepSeek-V3, 671B MoE trained for a reported ~$5.6M — 2024-12
